summary: The design is sound and stage 1's data supports a stage 2, but the change as written runs the self-check in a spawned child process, and muse_moe_w4a16/TASK.md says a submission that starts processes is rejected. Re-mint without the child process (stage 1 already ran this exact kernel in-process on the judge without a fault), and split Part B into stage 3 so this run reads only the slow-mode fix.
justification: The mechanism holds up. Stage 1 (job 1105a02aa3fa4e56) profiled moe_bs1_kernel at 37.7 us against the incumbent's 51.2 us of replaced kernels. The scored paired-ratio speedup at decode_1 (1.568) sits well above the speedup of medians (1.289), and the error grew from 0.47 to 1.29 us. That is what an uncorrelated two-mode distribution on our side looks like: when 41% of replays are fast and 59% slow, the median pair is a mixed fast+slow pair, giving about 85/56.5 = 1.5. So killing the slow mode is worth roughly 77/43 = 1.8-1.95x on decode_1 (vs master's 1.578). That is about +20% on that load and about +3.5% on the headline as a geomean over 6 loads, not the +16% stage 1 claimed. The ~42 us scored M2 target is plausible. The floor arithmetic is right: R is about 2 routes x ~27 MB per expert, about 55 MB, so 11.4 us at 4.8 TB/s, and 37.7 us is about 1.46 TB/s. M3 (18 us, ~3 TB/s) is physically reachable for a weight-stream GEMV with a deep cp.async ring on 132 SMs. WEAKEST LINK: the cause of the slow mode is assumed, not measured. The ~24 us extra is about one whole phase, which fits a chain stall, but it also fits a co-residency hazard. If any SM is briefly busy at launch (another stream's work, or the harness's L2-flush tail), one CTA starts late. Every phase-2 CTA that waits on its phase-1 tiles then stalls, and neither a tight poll nor item reordering fixes that. The planned timestamps (phase-1 start/end, phase-2 start) miss it. Record each CTA's entry globaltimer and %smid as well. The prepare-time self-check also replays with a warm L2 and nothing else on the GPU, so it may never reproduce the judge's slow mode. Write a buffer larger than L2 between the 100 self-check replays, the way the judge does. Second weak point: '128R items split in K to a multiple of 132' is not a free change. A K-split w13 tile needs its gate/up partials reduced before silu (silu is nonlinear), which adds a phase-1 ticket/reduction level and another place to stall. A simpler path to one wave is to size items so each CTA owns ceil(128R/132) whole tiles, and to have phase-2 CTAs take h chunks in the order they finish.
confounders: post-expert-norm-triton-small-m (gain): its _post_norm_combine_kernel is one of the replaced bs=1 kernels, so it is part of the incumbent that the fused kernel's row is compared against (3.1 us of 48.8). No interaction at runtime because num_tokens == 1 bypasses it entirely; nothing to disambiguate.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack (gain): supplies the _align_small path the fused kernel replaces at bs=1; bypassed at num_tokens == 1, so it does not confound the measurement, only defines the incumbent.
align-parallel-per-expert-verify (neutral, master): touches only num_tokens > 32; the bs=1 path is identical to stage 1's base, so the rebase changes nothing at decode_1.
marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm (gain): changes block_size_m only at num_tokens >= 128; disjoint.

In flight, not landed: stack-onewarp-hoisted-dispatchcombine(-from17) rewrites bs<=8 align and the bs<32 combine. If it lands first, the bs=1 incumbent drops by ~1-2 us, so read stage 2 against whatever master is at dispatch, not against the 51.2 us figure.
interference: No companion. This is a rewrite stage judged on the fused kernel's own profile row and the bs=1 replay distribution. Every landed hypothesis that touches bs=1 is bypassed when num_tokens == 1, so no ab-revert or ab-tune would change the reading. The one real attribution problem is internal: Part A (spin, one-wave and ordering) and Part B (deeper ring, K-split) in the same run would mix 'the slow mode is gone' with 'bandwidth went up'. The fix is to stage them, not to add a companion. Stage 2 = Part A plus the extended diagnostics. Stage 3 = Part B, minted only after stage 2's log shows which phase stalled and the replay distribution is unimodal.
rules_flags: BLOCKING: 'Run the self-check's first launches in a spawned child process' conflicts with muse_moe_w4a16/TASK.md Rules ('A submission is rejected if it ... starts processes'). Nothing in rules/ carves out an exception, and no submission with multiprocessing/subprocess has yet passed the judge's static check. That LESSONS entry came from a different kernel's createpolicy fault. Stage 1's moe_bs1_kernel (plain cp.async.cg, no createpolicy) already ran its self-check in-process on the judge cleanly, so drop the child process and keep the in-process try/except fallback. The same flag applies to the other queued 'childcheck' / child-process hypotheses across problems.

The bounded spin that 'sets an error flag and falls back' cannot fall back inside a timed graph replay, because there is no host branch on data. If it ever fires in timed calls, that call's output is wrong. Make the bound diagnostic only (use it to fail the prepare-time self-check), and set it far above any legitimate wait.

Unimodality assert (p90/p10 < 1.3) in prepare: if it fails and disables the fused path, the run silently measures master, which wastes the run. Print the distribution and keep the path; the judge's replays are the measurement. Also note the self-check's 100 graph replays are untimed prepare work, which is allowed (up to 300 s).

Debug timestamp buffer: record only in a self-check build or under a prepare-time flag. The timed kernel must not write the extra buffer or branch on its contents; a compile-time or kernel-arg flag set in prepare is fine.
Precision and caching are unchanged from stage 1 (NVFP4 kept lossless, BF16 y rounding matches master, epoch counters are state from prepare and not derived from inputs). OK.
open_questions: Is the slow mode a phase-2 spin/second-wave stall, or a late-starting CTA (an occupied SM at launch)? Per-CTA entry time + %smid decides it, and only if the self-check reproduces cold-L2, judge-like replays.

What is R at the judge's decode_1 seed? If R == 2 (256 phase-1 tiles over 132 CTAs), the second wave is nearly full and ordering helps; if R varies across the 5 tests, the one-wave sizing must cover R in 0..8.
Can the one-wave goal be met without a K-split of w13 tiles (which needs a pre-silu reduction), for example 2 whole tiles per CTA with phase-2 order matched to chunk completion?
Once a pre-flight check confirms the judge's static checker rejects multiprocessing, the LESSONS 2026-10-25 child-process advice should be amended for all problems.
